newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: POLL-PORTUGAL JULY CPI SEEN UP 1.7 TO 1.8 PCT Y/Y.
newsitem.headline: POLL-PORTUGAL JULY CPI SEEN UP 1.7 TO 1.8 PCT Y/Y.

text.p: Portugal's July consumer price index (CPI) is
expected to have risen by 1.7 to 1.8 percent
year-on-year, little changed from June's up 1.8 percent, according to a
Reuter poll of analysts.
Eight out of nine analysts at banks and brokerages predicted July CPI to stay flat or edge up 0.1 percent to produce a year-on-year rise of 1.7 to 1.8 percent. June CPI was down 0.3 percent.
But one analyst saw July CPI rising 0.2 percent, which would mean a 1.9-percent year-on-year increase.
The rolling 12-month average, the government's yardstick,
would be 2.7 percent under any of the predicted monthly
changes, down from June's 2.9 percent.
The government has forecast the rolling average to slow
to below 2.5 percent by year end.
The National Statistics Institute (INE) must issue the July
figures by next Thursday.

Analysts said July would be the last month CPI figures would benefit from the statistical impact of last year's sharp rise in meat prices caused by the madcow disease scare. Food and drink prices make up 45 percent of the index, and in June, this sector fell 0.9 percent year-on-year.
Following are analysts' forecasts for July's monthly rate:
